name: Heaven and Hell

date.source: Undated in the source; the fed's own archive index bills it as the very first card, and the fed's own in-show dialogue announces the 24 May 1998 Memorial Day Madness pay-per-view as still to come, bounding this show to shortly before that date.

notes: EWA's own first card, per archive.html's own listing. President Aaron announces an 8-man Extreme World Title tournament for Memorial Day Madness, drawing the field from a battle royal held the following two weeks.

matches.note: JD Freeman wins via DeathDrop onto a barbwire table.
Dave Slater wins via Hardcore DDT.

eliminations.note: Pinned via moonsault.
Counted out unconscious after being run into a guardrail.
Submitted to a Sharpshooter.
Pinned via 450 splash through a table.

matches.note: Jason Dragon wins by disqualification after Gorgeous George Gorg's interference; JellyFish Pete runs GGG off.
Served text: "Winner: None, Triple Count-out" — all three men counted out brawling.

name: Wednesday Night Warfare #1

date.source: Undated in the source; the fed's own archive index bills it as the second card, following Heaven and Hell.

matches.note: An electrified, razor-wire, tazer-rigged cage match. Ray Simmons wins via Doomsday Device.
DJ Friday wins after Flying Fury is shot dead through the forehead with an arrow bearing the initials "DR", mid-match, on live television.

eliminations.note: 450 splash to a chair, then thrown into an alligator pit at ringside.

matches.note: Rematch of heaven-and-hell's own triple count-out. Chance Charles wins via Extreme DDT.
Chris Douglas wins via The End of the Line. An unminted second man billed only as "Chris", accompanying Dragon, restrains and gropes Douglas's valet Honey before she cattle-prods him.
Johnny Sledge wins via Guillotine, his second match of the night.
A backstage-brawl-turned-city-street fight. Drifter wins via Highway Robbery.
LivKid wins via two Livingstones.
Served text: "Winner: No Contest... interference from a whole bunch of nosey busybodies" — LivKid, Tommy Grayson, and Ray Simmons all run in.

notes: EWA's own second card, per archive.html's own listing ("Monday Night War. The Pre PPV Spectacular" is a separate, later show — archive.html's own link labeled 'Monday Night Madness' resolves to wnw2.html, served here as monday-night-madness.html).

name: Monday Night Madness

date.source: Undated in the source; its own dialogue previews the 24 May 1998 (a Sunday) Memorial Day Madness pay-per-view as still to come, bounding this show to shortly before that date.

matches.note: Fought inside a barbwire-surrounded ring. Dave Slater wins via Hardcore DDT onto a ball of barbwire.
Suicide King wins via DDT with a stolen gas mask; Tommy Grayson interferes for LivKid and is himself locked in the chamber and gassed.
Ray Simmons wins via powerbomb off a 20-foot scaffold through a stack of tables.
SuperReactor wins via Gorilla Press onto a burning concession counter, with JD Freeman's help; Ray Simmons runs in afterward with a lead pipe on both winners.
Pimp Daddy J wins via Fireball; valets Diane and Silk are both dragged into the beating.

notes: EWA's own third card, billed in-show as 'Disasta in Nebraska.' President Aaron announces the Extreme World Title tournament field for Memorial Day Madness. Zaman is found chained in his own trailer's bathtub and apparently killed in an explosion staged live on the EXTREME-Tron — the second of the fed's own unsolved "DR" killings, after Flying Fury's (wnw-1).

name: Memorial Day Madness

date.source: Undated in the source; billed in Heaven and Hell's own dialogue as the fed's first pay-per-view, crowning its first Extreme World Champion, and previewed by name in Monday Night Madness and Wednesday Night Warfare #2's own dialogue as upcoming on 24 May 1998.

notes: The tournament that crowned JD Freeman the first EWA Extreme World Champion, held across Washington D.C. landmarks (the Kennedy Center, the Lincoln Memorial, the U.S. House of Representatives, the White House, the National Zoo, and a Capitol Hill bar). A National Zoo Gorilla Cage Match (billed as O'Lynch vs. Wolverine, neither a mintable figure) is decided when a masked man frees the gorillas mid-match and the gorilla Mopie wins the bout for the house via a three-slap count. A note signed "DR" — the same initials left at Flying Fury's on-screen killing (wnw-1) and Zaman's apparent bombing (monday-night-madness) — closes the show, congratulating and threatening the new champion.

matches.note: Pimp Daddy J wins via Bitch Slap. Extreme Eddy, disguised as an EMT, piledrives the injured Batchelder onto a chair after the bell.
A dark match at the Lincoln Memorial. Connor Chambers wins with a dive off the Lincoln statue's head that scores a double pinfall on both opponents at once.

eliminations.note: Squashed three-on-one in a car lot, then apparently crushed beneath a Ford eXtreme driven into the ring by JD Freeman; billed as LivKid's last EWA appearance, and played straight ("LivKid is dead!").

matches.note: Ray Simmons wins via Doomsday Device on Tommy Grayson. Jason Dragon, the Judge, Alistair Cloudfruit, Diablo, and two guest jobbers "borrowed from the DECWF" (Quicksilver, Hammer Canseco) work as lumberjack-enforcers around the cars; Fang runs in and fights off Quicksilver.
Bishop wins by sleeper hold, aided by a masked mystery man who dumps weapons into the ring. The Judge then invites Spyder to join his stable; Spyder refuses and is chair-shotted from behind.

matches.stipulation: Extreme World Title Tournament — Round One
matches.note: Staged in the U.S. House of Representatives with Newt Gingrich as guest referee. JD Freeman wins via a modified Texas cloverleaf ("the Devastator").

matches.stipulation: Extreme World Title Tournament — Round One
matches.note: Staged in the White House Oval Office and State Dining Room, with cameo introductions to Bill Clinton, Boris Yeltsin, Nelson Mandela, and Kuwait's Prince Nayef Abdul-Aziz. Chris Douglas wins via German suplex onto a teacart.

matches.stipulation: Extreme World Title Tournament — Round One
matches.note: Fought atop a weapon-laden scaffold. Tommy Grayson wins when Dave Slater falls off the scaffold through two tables.

matches.stipulation: Extreme World Title Tournament — Round One
matches.note: Fought in a shallow pool of salt water and lemon juice ringed with razor wire. Suicide King wins via a submerged figure four.
JD Freeman wins via Slingshot Extremeplex.
Fought through a Capitol Hill bar and pool hall. Chris Douglas wins via The End of the Line.

Fought bungee-corded inside an electrified cage ("the Thunderdome") with no referee and no rules. JD Freeman wins via a modified sleeper to become the first EWA Extreme World Champion. A note signed "DR" congratulates Freeman and threatens him next.

name: Wednesday Night Warfare, 3 June 1998
notes: EWA's own fourth card. Introduces the EWA Bitch's Championship, a self-styled, unsanctioned belt Pimp Daddy J claims for himself after nearly beating JD Freeman the week before — played for comedy throughout, never defended in a real match this run.

matches.note: Connor Chambers wins via Chamber-Made onto an upturned wagon.
Fought in the street outside the arena. Drifter wins via Highway Robbery through a car windshield.

Served text: "Once Again a No contest where Freeman is Involved." Douglas turns on Grayson mid-match to align with Freeman and SuperReactor as "Devastation Inc."; the three beat down a run-in named Justin Satiable (unminted, one-off) with a legbone.

Pimp Daddy J wins after Dirk Ryan runs in and beats down Ray Simmons with Pimp's own stick; Fang also runs in earlier to stop Pimp Daddy J from hitting Violet, after Pimp slaps her for trying to talk his valet Diane into leaving him.
A comedy brawl outside the ring (a beatnik cafe, a concession stand) ends in a triple count-out; Hanging Judge recruits Mopie into Jobbers Inc. afterward.

matches.stipulation: 20-Man Battle Royal (elevated ring) — inaugural EWA Television Championship

eliminations.note: First man thrown as the ring began to rise.
Elbowed over the top.
Back body dropped over the top.
Dropkicked from behind mid-throw.
Hoisted into the rafters by a noose (Mopie the Gorilla, directed by Hanging Judge and Alistair Cloudfruit from outside the match, worked the rope) and dropped roughly 150 feet, killed on impact.
Rappelled in unannounced partway through, immediately bulldogged over the top from 22 feet up by Pimp Daddy J — billed as killing Shawn B. on impact.

matches.note: The elevated ring's own cables snap partway through, tilting it and dropping several men early. Ray Simmons outlasts the field to become the first EWA Television Champion (matches reigns.json ewa-1998-tv-r001). Two deaths staged as real: Spyder (dropped from the rafters by Mopie) and Shawn Batchelder (bulldogged from the ring by Pimp Daddy J).

name: Wednesday Night Warfare, 10 June 1998

matches.note: Dirk Ryan's EWA debut. Wins via Critical Danger inside an exploding ring.
An impromptu Extreme World Title defense (Pimp Daddy J's own opponent, Bishop, no-showed). JD Freeman retains, both men going through flaming tables off a ladder.

matches.stipulation: Jobbers Inc. vs. Dragon/Anthony — guest referee Mopie the Gorilla
matches.note: Served text: "Dragon and Anthony via... the other guys losing." Mopie, refereeing, turns on his own Jobbers Inc. allies after Dragon steals his banana and counts them both out.
Fang wins via Lion's Roar.
An open challenge. Fang wins via Lion's Roar submission.
Chance Charles wins via a swinging DDT into a 450 splash.
Ray Simmons retains via Hardcore DDT.

notes: EWA's own fifth card, billed as a live special from Rochester.

name: Wednesday Night Warfare, 17 June 1998

matches.note: Verge Darsow's EWA debut. Wins via Lockdown chokeslam through a school bus roof.
Tommy Grayson wins via Showstopper, tossing Dirk Ryan off the scaffold.
Nigel Hayes wins by smashing a TV monitor over Irish Rebel's head.

Fang wins via Lion's Roar; Pimp Daddy J reveals a Death Row t-shirt mid-match but is not confirmed to have joined. Violet declines to beat the defeated, handcuffed Pimp Daddy J, then does anyway once he threatens her.
Ray Simmons wins via Doomsday Device onto a bed of nails.

matches.stipulation: Jobbers Inc. vs. New Breed — both men blindfolded
matches.note: Served text: "Winner: Ray Anthony via being DDT'd onto a steel chair" — Cloudfruit cheats out of his own blindfold, DDTs Anthony, then pins himself under Anthony's own arm so the ref (misreading the pin) raises Anthony's hand in a self-mocking loss.
Drifter wins via End of the Line, with Death Row members Pimp Daddy J, Cyris, and Verge Darsow interfering for him; JD Freeman and SuperReactor run in afterward to pull Douglas clear.

matches.stipulation: Five-Man Elimination — inaugural EWA North American Championship

eliminations.note: Combination 450 splash/Chamber-Made.
Scoop slam onto a turnbuckle explosive.
Boston Crab submission.
Suicide dive after a turnbuckle explosive.

matches.note: Connor Chambers wins and is named the first-ever EWA North American Cyber Champion by VP Artful.
A non-title match; Jason Dragon's manager Chris (unminted no relation to Chris Douglas) interferes, is knocked out by Chris Douglas. JD Freeman wins via Devastator.

notes: EWA's own sixth card. Connor Chambers is crowned the first EWA North American Champion here (17 June 1998) — see reigns.json's new ewa-1998-na-r000 row, which predates the previously-recorded first reign (Lonewolf, 13 September 1998, ewa-1998-na-r001); the title's own path between the two is not accounted for in this run's surviving record.

name: Wednesday Night Warfare, 15 July 1998

matches.note: Dingo, initially seconding Lonewolf, turns on him mid-match and hands Capital Punishment the win.
Connor Chambers wins via ankle lock submission.

Chance Charles wins via 450 splash, their third meeting; after the bell, Suicide King is speared in the forehead by Tommy Grayson, Christine Blossom is Liger Bombed by Grayson, and Simmons hits Charles with a Doomsday Device with Johnny Sledge's help.

Rob Riot wins via a Riot Squad finisher off a dumpster; Riot Squad members Helldorado and Rage interfere against Walker's own allies Dustin Warchild and Wayne "The Train" Rothschild, and Flame runs in afterward, newly aligned with the Riot Squad.
Dustin Warchild wins via Warblaster off a truck; Death Row (Cyris, Verge Darsow, O.G.) interferes for Drifter, and Warchild's own brother Devil Charger runs Drifter over with a car.

matches.stipulation: Barb Wire Death Match, EWA North American Cyber Championship
matches.note: Tommy Grayson retains via Showstopper. Grayson already holds the North American title entering this show — the title changed hands from Connor Chambers (won 17 June, ewa-1998-na-r000) to Grayson sometime before this card; the transition is not accounted for anywhere in this run's surviving record.

notes: EWA's own eighth card. Introduces the stable rivalry between Devastation Inc. (JD Freeman, Chris Douglas, SuperReactor) and the Innovators of Violence (Ray Simmons, Tommy Grayson, Johnny Sledge).

name: Wednesday Night Warfare, 5 August 1998

matches.note: Sean Foster wins after a llama kicks Rage in the mouth; a loose tiger and captive penguins both factor into the brawl.
Lonewolf wins via Midnight Howl, after Dingo bribes a fan to attack Steele.

eliminations.note: Chair-shotted over the top by an outside run-in (Demon).
Chair-shotted over the top by Billy Thompson.
Thrown over the top to the floor.
Face-Plant off the top rope onto a steel chair.

matches.note: Langdon Moore wins as the last man standing.
Wayne Rothschild wins by strapping Rob Riot into the electric chair and pulling the switch.

A late substitution for the injured Chris Douglas. Tommy Grayson wins via a new finisher, "The End" (a Kata Hajime submission), after two masked men (unidentified) beat down Death Row's own Cyris at ringside.

Suicide King retains via moonsault, with Jerry Micheals (a hidden IoV mole) interfering for Sledge before Wayne Rothschild runs in against both IoV men. Suicide King is already billed champion entering this show, and Devastation Inc.'s own Chris Douglas is separately referenced (in Tommy Grayson's own promo) as having previously taunted Suicide King during an earlier North American title defense against Grayson himself — the title's own path from Grayson (ewa-1998-na-r0005, defended 15 July) to Suicide King is not captured anywhere in the surviving record.

Fang retains — the served text rules the finish a disqualification (Helldorado runs in with a chair), and a DQ finish does not change a title; Fang is already billed television champion entering this show, and Miss Lisa (Capital Punishment's own valet) is thrown into a guardrail by Demon after the bell. Devastation Inc. and the Innovators of Violence brawl en masse afterward, alongside Death Row and the Riot Squad. The title's own path from Ray Simmons (ewa-1998-tv-r001, won 3 June) to Fang is not captured anywhere in the surviving record.

notes: EWA's own ninth card. A Shakespeare-parody dark match between stand-in actors playing the Riot Squad and Nate Walker (none of them the real wrestlers) ends when Bobo the Anti-Social Chimp kills all four in-fiction. Bushido (Stephen Daye and Jay Lange) debuts, beating down Rob Riot and Helldorado to claim newly-created EWA tag team titles from VP Artful before a mass Devastation Inc./Innovators of Violence/Death Row/Riot Squad brawl closes the show. JD Freeman announces he has become an EWA Vice President and will no longer wrestle, while keeping the Extreme World Championship.

name: Wednesday Night Warfare, 20 August 1998

matches.note: Capital Punishment wins by disqualification after a woman disguised as Miss Lisa hands the Train a brick, which he uses on Capital.
JD Freeman wins via Extreme-plex. Freeman brings a briefcase Violent Dark demands as "his belt" but it is never opened on-page.

Pimp Daddy J wins by disqualification after an unidentified masked man wearing a Death Row shirt runs in from under the ring to attack Drifter; Devastation Inc. runs in for the ensuing brawl. This masked man is never identified in the surviving record — distinct from the masked man unmasked as Pimp Daddy J himself at Bloodbath '98, since PDJ is a combatant in this same match.

eliminations.note: Dropkicked over the top rope to the floor.
Tossed over the top rope.
Distracted by valet Cassie Ripley setting Duke on fire, then pulled over the top rope.
Powerbombed through a table, leg-dropped, then thrown over the top rope by Cassie Ripley.

matches.note: Both remaining men, Roberts and Ripley, jump over the top rope simultaneously to eliminate themselves rather than face each other, leaving only Cassie Ripley in the ring; the fed's own text jokingly credits her as the winner, but no combatant remains to be declared one.
Chris Douglas wins via End of the Line.
Lasting Impression wins after Eaton, trying to break up a McManus pin attempt, accidentally levels his own partner with a leg drop.
Dean McGrath wins via Shaolin Sword.

Tommy Grayson wins by disqualification after Devastation Inc. (Chris Douglas, Connor Chambers, then JD Freeman disguised as a prison guard) interferes, and Wayne Rothschild — arriving seemingly to help Grayson with a cattle prod — instead reveals a Devastation Inc. shirt underneath his EWA shirt and turns on Grayson, joining the stable on-air.

notes: EWA's tenth card, its 4-month anniversary show. Wayne Rothschild's on-air heel turn to Devastation Inc. comes in the main event.

name: Wednesday Night Warfare, 12 August 1998

evidence.note: The fed's own archive index links a card ('wnw812.html') between the 5 August and 20 August Wednesday Night Warfare broadcasts, captioned 'Ahhh... another week, another death. Nobody expects the Spanish Inquisition' — the linked file was never captured in this holding.

notes: Falls between the served wnw-8 (5 August 1998) and wnw-9 (20 August 1998) broadcasts.

date.source: The fed's own archive index names the file 'wnw812.html', read as 12 August 1998 per the run's own MDD filename convention (e.g. 'wnw85' for 5 August, 'wnw820' for 20 August, both confirmed against their own served datelines).

name: Wednesday Night Warfare, 1 September 1998

evidence.note: The fed's own archive index links a card ('wnw91.html') after the 20 August Wednesday Night Warfare broadcast and before the 13 September Bloodbath '98 pay-per-view, captioned 'Hey... pull my finger. I got a surprise for ya!!' — the linked file was never captured in this holding.

notes: Falls between the served wnw-9 (20 August 1998) broadcast and the Bloodbath '98 pay-per-view (13 September 1998).

date.source: The fed's own archive index names the file 'wnw91.html', read as 1 September 1998 per the run's own MDD filename convention, positioned in the index between 20 August and the 13 September pay-per-view.

name: BloodBath '98

date.source: The fed's own archive index dates this pay-per-view 13 September 1998; the document itself carries no dateline of its own.

notes: EWA's second pay-per-view. Capital Punishment reveals a seven-man 'Team EWA' (himself, Chris Douglas, Wayne Rothschild, Tommy Grayson, Cyris, Johnny Sledge, JD Freeman) for a 7-on-7 Battle-Ground Tourney against a rival fed, the GWF, set for 1 October 1998.

matches.note: Billed "Cyris vs. Masked Superstar" — the masked man attacking Cyris on his own birthday unmasks as Pimp Daddy J. Capital Punishment runs in and chair-shots PDJ instead of helping him, letting Cyris pin him with the Death Sentence; Capital's own post-match promo frames it as payback for a disqualification incident at StableWars '98.

Billed on-page as "Original Krimez vs. Southern Pride," but Dawgbone's own introduction names the winning team "Partners in Krime," the newest addition to the Vicious Circle — the header appears to be a leftover mislabel.
O.G. Johnson wins with outside help from Wayne Rothschild, who beats Sanders with a bell while the referee is distracted, then offers O.G. a Devastation Inc. shirt afterward, unresolved on-page.
Drifter wins via Highway Robbery.
Violent Dark wins via German suplex onto broken table shards.
Capital Punishment kicks the plane's emergency door open and enziguris Scotty Jaguar out of it.

Bushido's own opponents are billed only as "Violence Inc.," their names withheld by the fed's own text ("whatever their names are, it's not THAT important") — not necessarily the same Darren Roberts/Adam Ripley pairing billed elsewhere under that name. Both opponents and the crossover jobber Scotty Jaguar, who falls from the sky mid-match, are killed when Jay Lange snaps Jaguar's neck and the other two are crushed; Stephen Daye is spared by his own opponents' own dropkick pushing him clear.

eliminations.note: Dropkicked through a wooden door.
Double leg drop through a thumbtack-covered glass table.

matches.note: Devastation Inc. wins as the I.R.O.N. cage explodes over both downed men.

Jeremy Taylor wins via a corkscrew Spike. Afterward, an unidentified man with a paper bag over his head attacks both men with a chair and spray-paints "G.P." in the ring before vanishing into the crowd — unresolved in the surviving record.
Kendall wins after Demon falls from the roof of the Pontiac Silverdome into a hovering helicopter's rotor blades.
Lonewolf wins the title via the Midnight Howl, with Dingo interfering twice to save him from a three-count.

matches.stipulation: Liquid Nitrogen Battle Royal (comedy costume match)
matches.note: WyldChylde pulls a lever flooding the caged ring with liquid nitrogen, then the tank itself breaks loose and crushes the ring and every entrant; the fed's own text jokingly credits "WyldChylde and the audience" rather than naming an in-ring winner.

name: Extreme Measures, 21 September 1998
notes: The first Extreme Measures broadcast, with Richard Riley filling in for an absent Jon Marx. Introduces Richard Riley (Dick) as new co-host and Devastation Inc.'s on-air power grab.

matches.note: Violent Dark wins with two Violent Vengeances. Afterward, "Bad Boy" Jeremy Taylor and valet Sweety Pie attack VD with a guitar and melted chocolate.
Daddy Desire wins via the Love Tap. Afterward, Tommy Grayson carves "IoV" into Slain's head with a razor for copying his "Extreme" gimmick.

The match is never resolved: four Devastation Inc. members (JD Freeman, Connor Chambers, Cyris, Wayne Rothschild) settle a game of rock-paper-scissors to decide who interferes, then Cyris and Wayne Rothschild beat down both wrestlers; JD Freeman uses the moment to declare Devastation Inc. is "taking over" the EWA.
Chris Douglas wins via Chi-Town Shocker onto a TV set's own remains. O.G. Johnson runs in for Drifter and is beaten down by Connor Chambers and Cyris until Wayne Rothschild breaks it up.

The Train wins the title via a pump-handle backbreaker after Johnny Sledge, asked by Lonewolf to intervene, instead chairs Lonewolf. Drifter hands the new champion a Death Row shirt afterward, left unexplained on-page.

matches.stipulation: Twelve-Man Rumble for the vacant, newly created EWA Global Hardcore Championship

eliminations.note: Accidentally caught by a brass-knuckle punch Drifter meant for Wayne Rothschild.
Both men eliminated together, tumbling over the top rope at once.

matches.note: Cyris becomes the true inaugural Global Hardcore Champion — two months before the previously-recorded first reign. Jerry Michaels and Dirk Ryan were originally announced but replaced (by O.G. Johnson and Jeremy Taylor) before the bell.

name: Extreme Measures, 25 September 1998
notes: Dirk Ryan announces his retirement on-air, citing a cocaine addiction dating to the SEWF's own end; JD Freeman declares Devastation Inc. holds the Global Hardcore and North American titles plus the fed's own vice presidency.

matches.note: Partners in Krime is awarded the win by forfeit after Lasting Impression fails to appear — their dressing room is found cleared out with a note. Cyris and Suicide King then beat down both Krime members afterward.
Violent Dark wins via Violent Vengeance.
Higor Rosa wins via the Confederate Crush after Daddy Desire, debuting the New Breed's own name, chairs Connor Chambers from behind.

Southern Pride wins after the Train interferes, belting Atrevido with the North American title and setting up the pin. Devastation Inc. then executes the stipulation on all four men: JD Freeman beheads Atrevido and runs a katana through Red Dragon, then poisons Southern Pride's own celebratory drink, killing Dangerous Duke and Psycho Paul as well.
Derek Davidson wins his debut via the Devil Driver off the second rope. The Train attacks Drifter with a chair and a DDT on the concrete afterward.
Dean McGrath and the Train win via McGrath's Too Bad For You, Ah?, with the Train tricking Sledge and Michaels into thinking McGrath might turn on his own partner.

matches.stipulation: Mystery Ladder Match for the EWA Television Championship
matches.note: President Aaron reveals Capital Punishment (not JD Freeman, whom Grayson expected) as Grayson's opponent for the newly unveiled "real" TV title. Capital Punishment wins the vacant title. Afterward, a masked martial-arts figure — later revealed as Gouki — attacks Capital Punishment and vanishes; WyldChylde then comically beats down Capital with a wiffle bat.

name: Extreme Measures, 4 October 1998
notes: Live from the Hartford Civic Center, with VP Artful as guest commentator.

matches.note: Dustin Madison wins his debut via frogsplash. Mike Paine attacks the beaten Deamon with a chair afterward.
Violent Dark wins via Violent Vengeance. Scott Johnson is then beaten down further in a stipulated open-challenge beatdown by the Train and Suicide King, who fake a handshake truce first.
Dawgbone wins via Superdawg, then sics his dog Ripp on Markov afterward.
Irish Rebel wins with heavy Innovators of Violence interference (Jerry Michaels, Capital Punishment, Tommy Grayson), then joins the stable on-air, given an IoV jersey.

The Train and Dean McGrath win via a Train Wreck after McGrath fakes a New Breed defection to fool Daddy Desire and Billy Thompson. Kenneth Morlock and Scott Johnson cut a hole through the ring floor to help their stablemates, but Train and McGrath escape.

Kenneth Morlock wins via figure-four with New Breed interference (Scott Johnson, Billy Thompson). A ten-man brawl (Douglas, Davidson, Morlock, Desire, Johnson, Thompson, Cyris, Suicide King, the Train, Capital Punishment) follows.
Suicide King wins with a men's-urinal shot, Chris Douglas assisting. New Breed (Billy Thompson, Scott Johnson) choke him out afterward.

matches.stipulation: Dumpster Match for the EWA North American Championship
matches.note: The Train retains, locking Drifter in the dumpster after both men fall in more than once.

matches.stipulation: surprise EWA Television Championship defense, no DQ, falls count anywhere
matches.note: Wyld tricks a bystander, Enrique, into making the winning cover on a beaten Capital Punishment; President Aaron immediately strips Enrique of the belt on the grounds he was never a legal participant and returns it to Capital Punishment. Afterward, a masked martial-arts figure calling himself Gouki attacks Capital Punishment, promising a rematch — the same figure who first appeared unnamed at the 25 September 1998 Extreme Measures, later revealed as Fang.

name: Extreme Tonight, October 1998

date.source: The filename ('et1013') and the fed's own archive index (which separately bills two October 'Extreme Tonight' dates) both point to mid-to-late October 1998; the document itself carries no clean dateline. Kept at month precision.

matches.note: Billed as Gouki's own in-ring debut; wins via frog splash.
Violent Dark wins his debut opponent via Violent Vengeance.
Suicide King wins via moonsault and his own urinal. Capital Punishment runs in afterward but is ambushed by Cyris, hiding under the ring with the Global Hardcore belt.
Dean McGrath wins via Shaolin Sword, earning Pimp Daddy J's valet Dianne for a week; Tommy Grayson, disguised as a cameraman, attacks McGrath and kisses Dianne afterward.
Jerry Michaels wins by playing possum for a chair-shot cover.
Ronny Wonder wins his EWA debut via a belly-to-back suplex bridge, helped by the cage's own electrified mesh.
The Train fails to appear (kayfabe-arrested); President Aaron strips him of the title on-air rather than award it to Daddy Desire by default, declaring it held up for the next Extreme Measures.

Tommy Grayson wins via piledriver after President Aaron turns on Devastation Inc., helping Grayson beat down Cyris with a belt shot, singapore canes, and pepper spray — an on-air alliance shift against DI.

notes: EWA's own Extreme Tonight premiere, re-airing matches from a preempted Extreme Measures.

name: Extreme Measures, 23 October 1998

date.source: The filename ('em1023') implies 23 October 1998; the document's own header reads simply 'Extreme Measures' with no explicit date. Kept at month precision.

matches.note: Eli Flair wins, both men knocked out by the finish and the referee counting regardless.
Dean McGrath wins via Too Bad For You, Ah? PDJ publicly slaps his own valet Dianne afterward for cheering McGrath on.
Cyris and Suicide King win a mystery-partner tag squash, ambushing Partners in Krime with chairs before the bell.
Never resolved as a match: the Train destroys Jerry Michaels's car, then ambushes and beats him with a pipe until security tasers him.
Fang's own in-ring return from his masked Gouki run; wins by reversing Cyris's Death Sentence into a huracanrana.

matches.stipulation: Battle Royal for the vacated EWA Global Hardcore Championship (last three eliminated go on to a three-way for the vacated North American and Television titles)

eliminations.note: Tangled with Lonewolf and both go over together.
Accidentally clotheslined over by his own stablemate.
Capital Punishment, Daddy Desire, Sid Seven, Leon Hayze, and Billy Thompson all go over the top together in one scrum after Tommy Grayson shoulder-blocks the group trying to eliminate Capital.
Both men eliminated together.

matches.note: Cyris wins his second Global Hardcore reign. Dean McGrath, Fang, and Ronny Wonder — the last three eliminated — immediately re-enter for the North American and Television titles below.

matches.stipulation: Three-way for the vacated EWA North American Championship
matches.note: Fang wins via German suplex bridge on McGrath.

matches.stipulation: Impromptu match for the vacated EWA Television Championship
matches.note: Immediately after the North American title match, Ronny Wonder rolls up a furious Dean McGrath for the vacant TV title.

notes: Billed on-air as the EWA's own relaunch under new power, with VP Artful publicly supplanting JD Freeman and President Aaron.

name: Extreme Tonight, late October 1998

date.source: The filename ('et1029') implies late October 1998; the document itself carries no clean dateline. Kept at month precision.

notes: An all-preview Extreme Tonight for Devil's Night — no matches air. VP Artful's own interview (conducted by Irish Rebel) discloses that Devastation Inc. was his own creation, run amok under JD Freeman, and that Aaron Michael and JD Freeman are both away from the promotion "for the moment."

name: Devil's Night '98

date.source: The fed's own archive index dates this pay-per-view 31 October 1998; the document itself opens on the Devil's Night logo with no separate dateline.

notes: EWA's third pay-per-view, live from Madison Square Garden.

matches.note: Sid Seven wins via DDT off the top rope.
Partners in Krime wins the Radium Junkees' own debut.
Pimp Daddy J wins, breaking his own Pimp Stick over Morlock's head for the pin.
Johnny Sledge wins via a face plant, with Wayne Rothschild's own ringside presence a factor.
Ronny Wonder wins via the Wonderful Ending.

matches.stipulation: Number-one contender's match for the EWA Global Hardcore Championship
matches.note: Eli Flair wins via the Extreme Corruption after Brett Anthony's own back gives out mid-cover.
Dean McGrath wins after Hellraiser, injured, taps out to a Shaolin Sword applied to Hellraiser rather than the Multinational Rebel.
Ronny Wonder deliberately submits and lays the belt over an unconscious Suicide King, handing him the title rather than losing it in a contested finish.

matches.stipulation: Cruiserweight tournament final, Cyris special guest referee
matches.note: Dean McGrath becomes the first EWA Cruiserweight Champion via Shaolin Sword, after Capital Punishment and the Train both interfere (the Train accidentally chairs his own ally Sledge instead of McGrath).

The Train wins via powerbomb after Jerry Michaels accidentally kills the Train's own girlfriend, Debra Delicious, with a chainsaw meant for him; Jerry suffers an apparent broken neck on the powerbomb.

Both men cover each other simultaneously on the final exchange; the referee counts the fall and raises Fang's arm, retaining the title — the fed's own text frames the finish as a fairness question rather than a declared double result.

name: Extreme Measures, 11 November 1998

matches.note: Maverick Matt Blanchard wins via a top-rope 450 splash.
Joker wins via a bowling-ball low blow and his Hocus Pocus knee drop.
Never resolved: Drifter runs in on both men with a chair, powerbombs and Highway Robberys Keaton, then cuts a promo declaring he is done being a fan favorite.

Touchdown Tommy wins via the Extra Point off the top rope, with Dawgbone and E-Legal Itaki interfering for Xavier. Johnny Sledge attacks Tommy afterward, challenging him to a Cage-Barbed Wire-Tasers match.
X-Tremist Revolution wins its own debut via Taylor's Bad Attitude.
Johnny Sledge retains by disqualification after Touchdown Tommy runs in for revenge and Detective Dee Brown arrests him mid-beatdown.
Ruled a double disqualification after Suicide King interferes for Cyris and Ronny Wonder runs in to help Flair, leaving all four men brawling.

notes: Five wrestlers make their EWA debuts on this card (Matt Blanchard, Joker, Cinergy, Travis Keaton, Touchdown Tommy).

name: Extreme Measures, 15 November 1998
notes: Two title changes (North American, Television) and Capital Punishment's on-air return to Devastation Inc.

matches.note: Vappa Mies forces a submission via a tilt-a-whirl backbreaker (billed "Total Domination"), then deliberately re-applies the hold on his own manager General Heimskur's signal, killing Derek Davidson on-air.
Mark Vizzack wins his own EWA debut (an open challenge after an anti-hardcore promo) via the Daredevil Flyer.
Violent Dark wins via Violent Vengeance. Drifter and Pimp Daddy J recruit him into Death Row afterward, handing him a Death Row t-shirt.
Maverick Matt Blanchard wins via Lights Out, distracting Touchdown Tommy with Johnny Sledge's own ringside appearance first.

Johnny Sledge wins by knocking Drifter off the scaffold into a pit of raw sewage. Pimp Daddy J and Violent Dark (newly Death Row) attack Sledge afterward until Tommy Grayson, his former Innovators of Violence stablemate, makes the save.
Pimp Daddy J wins after Drifter and Violent Dark interfere; Morlock is knocked unconscious rather than ever answering the ref's question.

matches.stipulation: Number-one contender's match for the EWA Global Hardcore Championship
matches.note: Ruled a disqualification win for Ronny Wonder after Cyris interferes; Cyris then publicly re-recruits Capital Punishment into Devastation Inc. as his own new "Enforcer," and tries to unmask Wonder before Eli Flair and EWA security intervene — Wonder's identity is left unresolved on-page.

matches.stipulation: Come As You Are Street Fight for the EWA North American Championship
matches.note: The Multinational Rebel wins the title via a small package. Afterward, taunted about his wife, Fang assaults the new champion until Violet reveals she is pregnant, not dying.

matches.stipulation: Texas Death Match for the EWA Television Championship
matches.note: Tommy Grayson wins the title, locking Suicide King in "The End" and outlasting the referee's ten count.

name: Extreme Measures, 22 November 1998
notes: Dan Dehart's own "Gentleman" John Charles cuts a promo threatening a WC-vs-EWA supercard. Devastation Inc. (Cyris, the Multinational Rebel, and two masked men) beats down Ronny Wonder in the men's room after his own #1 contender's loss, and Cyris nearly unmasks him before security and Eli Flair intervene.

matches.note: Dawgbone wins after blasting Serial Killer with a fireball, playing possum first.
Mark Vizzack wins via Daredevil Flyer.
Fang wins via Lion's Roar in his own comedic "bar fight" grudge match, then declares his only crime was beating Brown up.
Pimp Daddy J wins via Bitch Slap.
Suicide King wins via Greco-Roman toss, aided by Capital Punishment and Cyris using his own trademark urinal on Flair.
Death Row wins after Tommy Grayson abandons his own partner Johnny Sledge mid-match, walking out with manager Cindy Rossetti.
Blanchard wins the first fall (small package); Rebel wins the second (Irish Pride) and, with Capital Punishment interfering with a chair and the Judgement Drop, the third and the match.

Richard Riley, the scheduled challenger, does not appear; newly-named VP Wayne Rothschild invokes a contract clause forcing Cyris to defend against Ronny Wonder instead. Wonder wins via the Critical Danger and unmasks as Dirk Ryan. Dirk then has Richard Riley fall onto the discarded mask for a second, joke "pin" the announcer plays as a title change ("Winner and New EWA Global Hardcore Champion: Richard Riley??????") — not treated as a real reign.

name: December to Dismember '98

date.source: The document's own dateline reads 6 December 1998; the fed's own archive index separately bills this pay-per-view for 5 December 1998 — sources disagree by one day, both recorded.

notes: EWA's fourth pay-per-view, live from the New Orleans Superdome, with Crystal Laine (VP Rothschild's own broadcast partner) filling in for President Artful.

matches.note: Dee Brown wins via the Miranda Rights. "Deadly" Daelin Ashland debuts by attacking the victorious Brown afterward.
Death Row wins via a Pimp Slap off Drifter's shoulders onto Stanz. Violent Dark, not an official participant, helps Death Row by handing Pimp Daddy J his own Pimp Stick mid-match.
Ruled a no-contest after a masked interloper attacks both men and is unmasked as the Tyrant.
Johnny Sledge retains via the Wrecking Ball.

Tommy Grayson retains, using Johnny Sledge's own Wrecking Ball finisher on both Sledge (after Sledge saves Grayson from Death Row interference, then accidentally strikes Grayson's manager Cindy Rossetti) and Violent Dark.

matches.stipulation: EWA North American Championship Triple Threat
matches.note: The Multinational Rebel retains after Capital Punishment belts Eli Flair with the title itself. Cyris and the Rebel then reveal Capital Punishment's own recruitment into Devastation Inc. was a cruel prank, beating him down and expelling him; the mystic "Outlander" appears on the Extreme-Tron afterward, cursing Cyris and immolating his effigy.
Fang wins via the Lion's Roar. Afterward, Fang and Violet announce they are leaving the EWA for Kansas, ending Fang's own active in-ring run.

matches.stipulation: EWA Global Hardcore Championship, Steel Cage
matches.note: Cyris wins his third Global Hardcore reign via the Death Sentence, with a baseball bat smuggled in by the debuting Roadkill briefly turning the tide for Riley. Connor Chambers returns afterward, attacking Cyris to declare himself no longer aligned with Devastation Inc., before Dan Dehart, the WC's own former World Champion, arrives ringside and clashes with Suicide King.

name: Extreme Measures, 14 December 1998
notes: EWA's own show dedicated to "Nature Boy" Ric Flair. Dee Brown's own investigation into Lonewolf's death names JD Freeman as the man behind a string of hired-hitman EWA murders (Dingo, Johnathon Grayson, Lonewolf), and reveals Freeman himself was killed by the same hitman over an unpaid debt — Daelin Ashland cuts the interview short by attacking Brown.

matches.note: Myke Fury wins via Hell's Fury onto a VCR.
Dawgbone wins by count-out after Sarah and Daelin Ashland distract Roadkill.
Ruled a no-contest after Drifter and Pimp Daddy J run in on all three men.
Daelin Ashland wins via fisherman's suplex, then attacks Brown further after the bell until Riot Squad-badged security officers beat him off Brown.

Matt Blanchard wins the title after Tommy Grayson, disguised as a janitor, sabotages the match — piledriving Sledge's own wife Jessica and framing Sledge for the referee bump — then drapes Blanchard's arm over the downed champion.
Natural Criminals wins by powerbombing both Partners in Krime members through the cage floor's own hole onto broken glass.

matches.stipulation: Back Alley Brawl for the EWA Television Championship
matches.note: Tommy Grayson retains, with the Tyrant (unmasked after interfering) and then Cyris both factoring into the finish.
Eli Flair wins after the WC's own Outlander mysteriously interferes against both men before vanishing.

matches.stipulation: EWA Global Hardcore Championship, Ladder Match
matches.note: Cyris retains, climbing the ladder as Devastation Inc. runs interference against a returning Irish Rebel/Multinational Rebel-Suicide King skirmish at ringside.

name: Thursday Night Slaughter, 18 December 1998

matches.note: Ryland McCoy wins via a large package.
Shawn Griffin wins his own debut via a crucifix pin.
The All-Americans win via the Star Spangled Spike.
The Patriots win their own debut via a top-rope Spread Eagle Faceslam.
Roadkill wins via the Roadkill Stunner. "Deadly" Daelin Ashland attacks Roadkill afterward, continuing their feud.

Ruled a double disqualification in an eight-man brawl after Daelin Ashland — wearing a Death Row shirt — turns on his own new stablemate Tyrant, chairing him; Da Playa and "Gangsta" Jimmy Walker also run in.

notes: The debut episode's own text bills it "Friday Night Slaughter" and dates itself "Friday, December 18, 1998," hosted by the newly-installed VP Dirk Ryan and co-host Alexis Williams; VP Rothschild's own 14 December 1998 announcement of the new weekly show calls it "Thursday Night Slaughter," the name this show is filed under.

name: Extreme Measures, 23 December 1998

matches.note: Myke Fury wins via Fury's Hell.

Griffin's scheduled opponent never appears; Johnny Sledge substitutes and wins by disqualification after Tommy Grayson interferes. Griffin and Sledge then reveal themselves as the previously mysterious tag team Corporate Insurrection.

Dee Brown wins via a belly-to-belly suplex after head-butting his own bloodied forehead into Flair's face. Devastation Inc. (Cyris, the Multinational Rebel, two masked men) beats Brown down again backstage afterward.
Roadkill wins via the Roadkill Stunner, both men fighting through a parking lot of cars.
Death Row wins via the Social Outcast, with Tyrant and Dawgbone factoring in at ringside.
Elite from the Street wins after Pimp Daddy J taps out to a bull-rope choke.

matches.stipulation: Steel Cage Match, Johnny Sledge special guest referee
matches.note: Devastation Inc. wins after Tommy Grayson turns on his own partner Suicide King mid-match, joining Cyris and the Multinational Rebel; Grayson then attacks the wheelchair-bound VP Wayne Rothschild when Rothschild tries to intervene in Cyris's own post-retirement Global title plans.

notes: Cyris announces a "lethal lottery" clause in his own contract letting him name his next Global Hardcore challenger; Dawgbone is drawn, set for a barbed-wire dog collar match. Jerry Micheals reveals himself as the returning, masked Riot Squad member Helldorado, and Rob Riot also resurfaces.

name: Extreme Measures, 30 December 1998
notes: VP Rothschild announces the main event of Yuletide Beatings: Tommy Grayson vs. Cyris for the Global Hardcore Championship (no DQ, no count-out, must have a winner) and the Multinational Rebel defending the North American title against Matt Blanchard.

matches.note: Myke Fury wins via Fury's Hell.
Elite from the Street wins via a small package.
Matt Blanchard wins an open challenge via a new version of Lights Out (a Dragon Sleeper). The Multinational Rebel attacks Blanchard from behind afterward.
The South Syndicate Soldiers win by overturned decision: Riot Squad's own Rage interferes to win the match outright, but VP Rothschild reverses the result on-air.
Tyrant wins via the Payoff, with Roadkill and Drifter both factoring in from ringside.
Corporate Insurrection scores an upset win over the #2 seed via the Hostile Takeover.
Roadkill wins the title, with Johnny Sledge's interference the deciding factor.
The Multinational Rebel retains with a masked Devastation Inc. member's interference.

matches.stipulation: EWA Global Hardcore Championship, Dog Collar Match
matches.note: Cyris retains after Tommy Grayson trips Dawgbone during a turnbuckle-touching endurance spot.

name: Yuletide Beatings
notes: EWA's fifth pay-per-view, live from Seattle's Kingdome. Crystal Laine is murdered in the ring — her throat cut — during a botched entrance meant for another wrestler, "Fox" Hans Taubmann, who is questioned but not charged on-page. The WC's Dan Dehart and Merlin "g-Crusher" challenge Devastation Inc. to a crossover tag match. The Warlord turns on his own manager General Heimskur, revealing his real name as John Davis.

matches.note: Dawgbone wins via a Ghetto Driver into the Superdawg.
Simply Irresistible wins its own debut via a Stun Gun DDT.
Shawn Griffin wins via the Nightlight. Peter Damien attacks the beaten Da Playa afterward with tortilla chips and salsa.
Shawn Foster wins the title via the Natural Death, his own tag partner Natural Born Killah pulling Violent Dark off the ropes to even the odds.
Roadkill retains via the Roadkill Stunner.
Johnny Sledge wins the title via a guillotine leg drop, with Shawn Griffin fending off Tommy Grayson's own interference attempt at ringside.
Death Row wins the vacant EWA World Tag Team Championship via the Social Outcast, with Tyrant and Dawgbone interfering from ringside.

matches.stipulation: EWA Global Hardcore Championship, one-hour time limit
matches.note: The match never happens: Cyris announces his own retirement from wrestling on-air, recapping his three Global Hardcore reigns and disbanding Devastation Inc. by handing the EWA over to Death Row. Grayson attacks the wheelchair-bound VP Wayne Rothschild when told the vacant title's format is still undecided; Cyris pulls Grayson off Rothschild and the two shake hands, closing the show as Grayson storms off.

name: Extreme Measures, 6 January 1999
notes: VP Rothschild announces his engagement to Crystal Laine on-air. Devastation Inc. (Cyris, the Multinational Rebel, Tommy Grayson) ambushes Shawn Griffin in the parking lot before the show.

matches.note: Dr. Silver wins his own EWA debut via the White Trash Wipeout.
Fox wins his own debut via the Bloodchiller, then refuses to release the hold after the bell, dislocating Welsh's shoulder before security drags him off.
Death Row advances via the Social Outcast.

South Syndicate Soldiers advances after an injured Shawn Griffin, still recovering from a pre-show Devastation Inc. attack, makes an ill-advised tag; Roadkill runs in briefly to help Sledge but the numbers advantage tells.
Tyrant wins the title after the Multinational Rebel chairs Blanchard from behind.

name: Thursday Night Slaughter, 21 January 1999

matches.note: Peter Damien wins by disqualification after Da Playa runs in and attacks him.
The Warlord, now billed John Davis, wins via Total Domination.
Bunghole Boys wins its own debut via the Fart Knocker Double Inverted Powerbomb.
g-Crusher wins via his own submission finisher.
Jason Moore wins his own EWA debut via the Kansas Jam.
Daddy Desire wins via the Love Tap. Matt Allen attacks the celebrating Desire afterward, until Kenneth Morlock — revealed as Desire's own brother — runs in to make the save.
"Super Duper" Gary Cooper wins via the Super Duper Slam.
Westside Walavan wins via the Westside Bomb.
Elite from the Street wins the main event; Death Row (Drifter, Tyrant, Violent Dark, Dawgbone) storms the ring afterward and beats down both winners.

notes: Taped at the Tacoma Dome; presented as quick, abbreviated match results without the usual announcer banter.

name: Extreme Measures, 18 January 1999
notes: Daddy Desire and Kenneth Morlock (revealed as brothers) beat down Matt Allen, ending the South Syndicate Soldiers. Eli Flair and Poison Ivy return from injury, calling out both Cyris and Dr. Silver.

matches.note: Dan Dehart wins his own EWA debut via the Final Destruction. His own partner g-Crusher beats the loser down with a lead pipe afterward.
Tyrant wins with Drifter and Dawgbone's own interference.
Dr. Silver wins by disqualification after Fox refuses to stop hitting him with a chair, then attacks the referee too; Riot Squad-badged security officers finally beat Fox off with nightsticks.
Ruled a disqualification after Tyrant interferes for Da Playa against Foster's own partner Natural Born Killah; Foster retains.
Drifter, the reigning tag team champion, wins via the Social Outcast.
Roadkill retains after Pimp Daddy J, running in with the rest of Death Row, accidentally strikes his own stablemate Dawgbone.
Johnny Sledge retains via the Wrecking Ball.
Tommy Grayson wins after his own manager Honey slips him a foreign object, then locks on The End.

name: StableWars '98

date.source: The fed's own archive index bills this as a 1998 special; the document itself carries no exact dateline. Kept at year precision.

matches.note: Billed "Irish Rebel" here; wins after both men (and the drunken referee) are left barely conscious.
Helldorado wins via a rack slam onto a steel chair.

Cyris wins by disqualification after an unidentified masked man runs in from the crowd and attacks him with a nightstick — the same description ("the masked man that attacked Cyris") wnw-8 later cites as happening "during the last PPV," placing this show before that broadcast. Rob Riot invites the beaten Capital Punishment to join the Riot Squad afterward.

Suicide King wins the title via the Sharpshooter. Scotty Jaguar, debuting as a new Innovators of Violence member, attacks the victorious Suicide King afterward before a mystery man (revealed as "a Wild Horse," i.e. Jay Lange) runs in, reclaiming a stolen DECWF title belt from Jaguar.
Lonewolf wins via the Midnight Howl.
Lonewolf wins via a roll-up.
Capital Punishment wins after the Riot Squad (Rob Riot, Rage, Helldorado) interferes, laying Capital Punishment over the exhausted Lonewolf for the pin.

matches.stipulation: Eight-Man Battle Royal, Riot Squad vs. Nate Walker's team

eliminations.note: A Warblaster sent him over the top rope through a table.
Clotheslined over the top; Jamie stood in for Fang, the announced mystery partner, who arrived in street clothes and refused to wrestle.
Eliminated herself, jumping over the top rope unprompted.
Struck with a crutch.
Thrown out onto the ring announcer.
Pushed off the turnbuckle to the floor.
Eliminated himself, jumping over the top rope rather than continue against Rob Riot.

matches.note: Capital Punishment, not an announced entrant, joins the match by attacking Nate Walker mid-bout and revealing a Riot Squad shirt underneath his own gear, before withdrawing when Flame and Dustin Warchild arrive to "handle" Nate Walker's side. Rob Riot alone remains in the ring at the finish, Rage and Helldorado already eliminated and Capital Punishment having withdrawn earlier; the fed's own text still credits the win to "Riot Squad" as a team.

matches.stipulation: Stable War: a heated glass cage over two joined rings, submission only
matches.note: Devastation Inc. wins after Cyris — supposedly on Death Row's side — reveals himself as JD Freeman's own planted traitor, blindsiding Verge Darsow and joining Devastation Inc. on the spot. An unidentified masked man in a black jumpsuit runs in earlier to help Death Row against DI, only to be turned on by Cyris as well once the reveal happens; his own identity is never resolved on-page.

notes: A four-way commentary booth (Jim Smith, Crystal Laine, and a distracted guest VP Artful) calls the show. JD Freeman closes the broadcast by producing a contract clause that forces President Aaron to name him Vice President on-air — the beginning of Devastation Inc.'s own rise to power. Cyris's own turn here is the moment his later retirement speech (Yuletide Beatings) calls "the pinnacle" of his jump from Death Row to DI.

name: Extreme Measures, 24 May 1999 (the EWA's relaunch card)

evidence.note: The fed's own preview page bills a full 15-match card, including a battle royal main event, for Monday 24 May 1999 at Madison Square Garden.

Every wrestler on the relaunch roster carries exactly one recorded match by the time this page was captured (3 June 1999), consistent with this being their only card since the relaunch — the results page itself was never captured.

notes: The card the fed's own site was actively promoting when this snapshot was taken; no results page survives in this capture.

date.source: The fed's own preview page bills the card for Monday, 24 May 1999 (promotions/ewa-1998/archive/upcoming-events.html).
